probes.query: The allocator deliberately staggers allocations to avoid cache aliasing (everything landing at the same address mod 2K). Where is the cyclic alignment offset computed for that?
expectedFacts: NextAlignedOffset returns a cyclic offset that is a multiple of kAlignment, advancing an atomic counter mod kGroups (kAlias/kAlignment) so successive allocations are staggered to reduce cache aliasing on x86
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: Behavioral (why, not just where). Verified: grep -n 'size_t NextAlignedOffset' hwy/aligned_allocator.cc -> aligned_allocator.cc:57; comment 'Returns a random (cyclical) offset for AllocateAlignedBytes' at :56; uses atomic next.fetch_add % kGroups (:62), kAlias rationale comment at :40-42 ('aliasing can only occur at multiples of 2K').

probes.author: kotlin-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'public fun handleCoroutineException' CoroutineExceptionHandler.kt -> CoroutineExceptionHandler.kt:18; body looks up `context[CoroutineExceptionHandler]?.let { it.handleException(...) ; return }` then falls back to handleUncaughtCoroutineException (lines 18-32). Caller: AbstractCoroutine.kt:115-117 `handleOnCompletionException(exception) { handleCoroutineException(context, exception) }`. Standalone coroutines from launch are AbstractCoroutine subclasses. HARD: the dispatch is via a CoroutineContext.Element key lookup (context[CoroutineExceptionHandler]) plus a global fallback — not a direct call edge; spans two files and a context-keyed indirection.

expectedFacts: The err_message! macro calls crate::messages::set_errored() and then delegates to message!, which (if messages are enabled) expands to eprintln_locked! — so err_message! is a three-macro chain (err_message -> message -> eprintln_locked) that prints the 'rg: ' prefix to stderr
probes.author: rust-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'macro_rules! err_message' crates/core/messages.rs -> messages.rs:82. err_message! (msgs.rs:82-87) calls set_errored() then message!; message! (msgs.rs:71-78) calls eprintln_locked!; eprintln_locked! (msgs.rs:33) writes 'rg: ' prefix. HARD: the answer is a #[macro_export] macro_rules! definition, not a fn — symbol search keyed on 'errored flag'+'non-fatal error' must resolve the macro, and the behaviour spans a 3-macro expansion chain that lexical/AST tools struggle to follow.
